title: Weighted CNF SAT by required satisfying weight
task: Can exactly k variables be set to true in a satisfying assignment?
encoding: An explicit CNF formula over a declared finite variable set and a nonnegative integer k.

qualifications: The theorem also holds under k ≤ μ(r) for each nondecreasing unbounded function μ as in the source.

sources.locator: Theorem 3.5, pp. 225–227 (earlier bound without a parameter factor)

reader.label: Sublinear exponent in the candidate count

bounds.statement: Under FPT ≠ W[1], no deterministic algorithm solves Weighted CNF SAT within the stated running time.

qualifications: The source states this bound under the positive-rate SNP premise, which follows from ETH by sparsification.
The theorem also holds under k ≤ μ(M) for each nondecreasing unbounded function μ as in the source.

reader.label: Sublinear exponent in the full encoding length

bounds.statement: Under ETH, no deterministic algorithm solves Weighted CNF SAT within the stated running time.

reader.boundContext: The required satisfying weight k. Here f denotes arbitrary total computable parameter function, r denotes number of variables, M denotes complete source encoding length.

recoveryDispositions.reason: The number of variables r can be smaller than the full encoding length M. The exact source comparison does not establish the bound measured only in M.
